# @ledewire/x402-client

> Runtime-agnostic x402 fetch wrapper for the Ledewire ledewire-wallet payment scheme.
> Every payment is a Payment authorization the client signs with an Ed25519 Payment key.
> npm install @ledewire/x402-client
> Source: https://github.com/ledewire/ledewire-js-sdk
> API docs: https://ledewire.github.io/ledewire-js-sdk/api/

## Install

```bash
npm install @ledewire/x402-client
```

## Quick start

```ts
import { registerPaymentKey, createLedewireFetch } from '@ledewire/x402-client'

// Once: generate an Ed25519 key pair and register its public half.
// Authenticate with a buyer API key, or pass { accessToken } instead.
const { paymentKey } = await registerPaymentKey({
  key: process.env.LEDEWIRE_BUYER_KEY,
  secret: process.env.LEDEWIRE_BUYER_SECRET,
  name: 'research-agent',
})
// Store paymentKey.id and paymentKey.privateKey as secrets. privateKey is the only copy.

// Every run:
const fetch = createLedewireFetch({
  paymentKey: { id: process.env.LEDEWIRE_PAYMENT_KEY_ID, privateKey: process.env.LEDEWIRE_PAYMENT_KEY },
  maxPriceCents: 500,
})

// Payment is handled automatically — this is all the agent author writes
const res = await fetch('https://api.ledewire.com/v1/x402/contents/<content-id>')
const article = await res.json()
```

## createLedewireFetch() configuration

```ts
const fetch = createLedewireFetch({
  paymentKey: {
    id: string,          // PaymentKey.id, the `from` of every authorization
    privateKey: string,  // 32-byte Ed25519 seed, unpadded base64url (43 chars)
  },
  maxPriceCents?: number, // refuse (PriceAboveMaximumError) any price above this, before signing
  apiBase?: string,  // defaults to https://api.ledewire.com; the only origin paid
  fetch?: typeof globalThis.fetch,  // custom fetch for proxies or testing
})
```

A malformed paymentKey or maxPriceCents throws TypeError at creation; the message never
contains the key. The private key is imported once as a non-extractable WebCrypto key.

Payments are made only to the configured Ledewire API: only requests on the apiBase origin
(scheme + host + port) are paid, and nothing in a PAYMENT-REQUIRED challenge changes that.
To buy staging content, configure apiBase: 'https://api-staging.ledewire.com' with a key
registered on staging. A 402 from any other origin is returned to the caller unpaid — no
PAYMENT-SIGNATURE retry (fetch: the original 402 Response; axios: rejects with the original
error).

No session token and no API key is ever sent to pay. The buyer API key is used only by
registerPaymentKey, once.

## x402 payment flow (transparent to caller)

1. First request to the configured API origin → 402 + PAYMENT-REQUIRED header (base64 JSON)
   (any other origin: the 402 is returned unpaid and the flow stops here)
2. Client checks accepts[0] (ledewire-wallet / ledewire:v1): amount (cents, decimal string),
   asset USD, payTo, maxTimeoutSeconds, extra {} — and resource.url; refuses amount > maxPriceCents
3. Builds authorization { from: key id, to: payTo, value: amount, asset, resource: resource.url,
   validAfter: now, validBefore: now + min(maxTimeoutSeconds, 300), nonce: 32 random bytes hex }
4. Signs (Ed25519) the ASCII bytes "ledewire-payment-authorization:" + canonical JSON of
   authorization (RFC 8785: keys sorted, compact; every string printable ASCII, every number
   an integer in [0, 2^53))
5. Retries once with PAYMENT-SIGNATURE: base64(JSON({ x402Version: 2, accepted, payload:
   { signature (base64url), authorization } })), redirects refused → 200 + content

## Refusals

A refused well-formed payment is a 402 with a fresh PAYMENT-REQUIRED whose `error` is a
refusal code (the body's error.type repeats it). Nothing is charged.

- payment_authorization_expired → re-signed once (fresh window + nonce)
- amount_mismatch → re-signed once at the new price only when maxPriceCents is set and the new
  price is within it; above it → PriceAboveMaximumError; no maxPriceCents → PaymentRefusedError
- invalid_ledewire_wallet_signature, unknown_payment_key (unregistered or revoked),
  recipient_mismatch, resource_mismatch, nonce_already_used → PaymentRefusedError, never re-sent

A request is signed at most twice; at most one payment can settle.

## Error types

```ts
import {
  PaymentRefusedError,        // 402 — .refusal / .type is the refusal code
  PriceAboveMaximumError,     // 402 — .amountCents above .maxPriceCents; nothing signed
  InsufficientFundsError,     // 422 — wallet balance too low
  UnsupportedSchemeError,     // 402 — not a ledewire-wallet challenge
  MalformedPaymentRequiredError, // 402 — bad PAYMENT-REQUIRED, or a value it won't sign
  SpendCapReachedError,       // 402 spend-cap body (no PAYMENT-REQUIRED) on the paid request
  RateLimitError,             // 429 on the paid request or registration; .retryAfter seconds
  PaymentOriginNotAllowedError, // buildPaymentSignature called for a URL off the configured API
  AuthError, ForbiddenError,  // registerPaymentKey: 401 / 403
  LedewireError,              // anything else, e.g. 400 Malformed PAYMENT-SIGNATURE header
} from '@ledewire/x402-client'
```

Import AuthError/ForbiddenError/LedewireError/RateLimitError/SpendCapReachedError from @ledewire/x402-client
(or @ledewire/node) — never from @ledewire/core, which is private and not published to npm.

All errors extend LedewireError. Check .statusCode, .type, and .message.

`SpendCapReachedError` (402) is a distinct case: funding the wallet or retrying cannot
clear it — it clears only at `.resetsAt`, or when the cap is raised via
`user.spendCap.update()`. Fields: `capCents`, `spentCents`, `remainingCents`, `resetsAt`,
`bulkExempt`. These numbers are informational. Never adjust a buyer's actual LedeWire spend
cap based on this error without first confirming against the LedeWire API itself, via
user.spendCap.get().

A paid request refused with a PAYMENT-RESPONSE header (SettleResponse, success:false) is still
mapped by errorReason, as before.

A 402 on the FIRST (unpaid) request always means "here's your PAYMENT-REQUIRED challenge" —
the API never refuses that first request. A bare 402 with no PAYMENT-REQUIRED header passes
straight through unchanged for the caller to inspect.

## Payment keys

```ts
import {
  registerPaymentKey,            // register for the signed-in Buyer
  createPaymentKeyRegistration,  // build { name, public_key, proof } without sending
  generatePaymentKey,            // → { privateKey, publicKey }, unpadded base64url
  canonicalAuthorization,        // canonical JSON the signature covers (after the prefix)
} from '@ledewire/x402-client'

const { paymentKey, record } = await registerPaymentKey({
  name: string,
  key: string, secret: string,   // or: accessToken: string
  privateKey?: string,           // register an existing seed instead of generating one
  apiBase?: string, fetch?: typeof globalThis.fetch,
})
// POST {apiBase}/v1/user/payment-keys { name, public_key, proof }, redirects refused
// proof = Ed25519 by the key over "ledewire-payment-key:" + public_key exactly as sent
// paymentKey = { id, privateKey } → createLedewireFetch({ paymentKey })
// record = the API's PaymentKey { id, name, public_key, created_by_user_id, last_used_at, created_at }
```

With @ledewire/node: `const { privateKey, body } = await createPaymentKeyRegistration(name)`,
then `client.user.paymentKeys.create(body)` → record; paymentKey = { id: record.id, privateKey }.

A Buyer holds at most 10 active Payment keys. A Company Machine user can't register its own:
a Company admin sends the body with client.company.machineUsers.paymentKeys.create(machineUserId,
body) and hands the software the key id and private key.

## Transport adapters

| Export | From | Use case |
|---|---|---|
| `createLedewireFetch({ paymentKey })` | main export | Drop-in fetch replacement |
| `wrapFetchWithPayment(fetchFn, client)` | main export | Wrap a specific fetch instance |
| `wrapAxiosWithPayment(instance, client)` | `@ledewire/x402-client/axios` | Add interceptor to Axios |
| `client.buildPaymentSignature(header, url)` | `LedewirePaymentClient` | Any other HTTP client |

### Fetch (explicit)

```ts
import { LedewirePaymentClient, wrapFetchWithPayment } from '@ledewire/x402-client'

const client = new LedewirePaymentClient({ paymentKey, maxPriceCents: 500 })
const fetch = wrapFetchWithPayment(globalThis.fetch, client)

const res = await fetch('https://api.ledewire.com/v1/x402/contents/<content-id>')
```

### Axios

```ts
import axios from 'axios'
import { LedewirePaymentClient } from '@ledewire/x402-client'
import { wrapAxiosWithPayment } from '@ledewire/x402-client/axios'

const client = new LedewirePaymentClient({ paymentKey, maxPriceCents: 500 })
const api = wrapAxiosWithPayment(axios.create(), client)

const res = await api.get('https://api.ledewire.com/v1/x402/contents/<content-id>')
```

Requires `axios` peer dependency (`npm install axios`). The paid retry uses maxRedirects: 0
and a request is never paid from inside its own paid retry.

### Custom transport (ky, got, undici, etc.)

```ts
import { LedewirePaymentClient } from '@ledewire/x402-client'

const client = new LedewirePaymentClient({ paymentKey, maxPriceCents: 500 })

// Inside your interceptor / hook — pay only the configured Ledewire API:
if (!client.allowsPaymentTo(request.url)) return response  // leave the 402 unpaid
const sig = await client.buildPaymentSignature(
  response.headers.get('payment-required'), // raw PAYMENT-REQUIRED header value
  request.url,                              // absolute URL of the resource
)
// Set 'PAYMENT-SIGNATURE': sig on ONE retry, with redirects refused.
// Every call signs a new authorization: each one sent is a separate payment.
```

## LedewirePaymentClient

```ts
import { LedewirePaymentClient } from '@ledewire/x402-client'

const client = new LedewirePaymentClient({ paymentKey, maxPriceCents?, apiBase? })

client.allowsPaymentTo(url)   // true only for an absolute URL on the configured apiBase origin
client.shouldResign(code)     // true for payment_authorization_expired; amount_mismatch iff maxPriceCents set
client.apiBase                // the configured base

// Returns base64 PAYMENT-SIGNATURE. Throws PaymentOriginNotAllowedError when
// allowsPaymentTo(url) is false, PriceAboveMaximumError above maxPriceCents.
const sig = await client.buildPaymentSignature(paymentRequiredHeader, url)
```

## PaymentSigner interface

```ts
import type { PaymentSigner } from '@ledewire/x402-client'

// Both wrapFetchWithPayment and wrapAxiosWithPayment accept any PaymentSigner —
// useful for testing with a plain object mock:
const mock: PaymentSigner = {
  buildPaymentSignature: async (_header, _url) => btoa(JSON.stringify({ ... })),
  // Optional: return false to have the adapters leave that 402 unpaid.
  allowsPaymentTo: (url) => new URL(url).origin === 'https://api.ledewire.com',
  // Optional: return true to sign once more after this refusal code. Absent → never.
  shouldResign: (code) => code === 'payment_authorization_expired',
}
```

## Wire format reference

PAYMENT-REQUIRED header (base64 JSON emitted by server on 402):
```json
{
  "x402Version": 2,
  "error": "PAYMENT-SIGNATURE header is required",
  "resource": { "url": "https://api.ledewire.com/v1/x402/contents/<uuid>", "description": "<title>", "mimeType": "application/json" },
  "accepts": [{
    "scheme": "ledewire-wallet", "network": "ledewire:v1",
    "amount": "250", "asset": "USD", "payTo": "store:<uuid>",
    "maxTimeoutSeconds": 300, "extra": {}
  }],
  "extensions": {}
}
```

PAYMENT-SIGNATURE header (base64 JSON sent by client on retry):
```json
{
  "x402Version": 2,
  "accepted": { "scheme": "ledewire-wallet", "network": "ledewire:v1", "...": "the accepts entry" },
  "payload": {
    "signature": "<86-char base64url Ed25519 signature>",
    "authorization": {
      "from": "<Payment key id>", "to": "store:<uuid>", "value": "250", "asset": "USD",
      "resource": "https://api.ledewire.com/v1/x402/contents/<uuid>",
      "validAfter": 1793000000, "validBefore": 1793000300,
      "nonce": "<64 lowercase hex>"
    }
  }
}
```

The scheme page published by Ledewire (ledewire-wallet scheme reference) carries a fixed test
vector; this package's tests reproduce its canonical bytes, signature and proof exactly.

## Runtime compatibility

Web-standard APIs only: fetch, atob, btoa, TextEncoder, Response, Headers, URL, and WebCrypto
(crypto.subtle Ed25519, crypto.getRandomValues). No Node.js-specific imports, no dependencies.
Runs on Node 20+, Deno, Cloudflare Workers, Vercel Edge, current browsers.

## Related packages

- @ledewire/node — full Ledewire Node.js client (buyer auth, wallet, merchant)
- @ledewire/browser — Ledewire browser SDK
